title: kohane-index-desuno: an LLM/API-friendly standalone indexer with a Rust core

goals.title: Standalone software with the mim lineage: memory and indexing, an LLM/API-friendly surface, wide planned integration
goals.notes: KID began as a generalisation of mim and keeps its memory-and-index bloodline, but it is an independent piece of software now: one engine (16 model-facing tools), one CLI, one MCP surface. This is the root of the plan; every goal below names the files it touches and the suite that judges it.

goals.title: The language plan is settled: a Rust single core, a JS thin shell, the C# workstation unchanged
goals.notes: Rust carries the engine, decoders, DSP and judges (one binary, MCP and CLI entries, same-source WASM); JS keeps only the DSH plugin thin shell as a process bridge; the C# WinUI workstation stays on the HTTP bridge. Migration is stage-by-stage, never big-bang: decoder kernel first, then the tool surface, then the shell. research/ probes stay JS and are not migrated.

goals.title: The Rust decoder kernel, complete: ADPCM, FLAC, sf2, fxp, lm4, the kb-media containers, kba, kbb, kbi, ztdw and the mix renderer all byte-exact with the JS originals
goals.notes: The whole decoder family is ported under law 9 cross-reading. Byte-exact where the format allows it: ADPCM and FLAC encoders match the JS streams, sf2/fxp/lm4 parsers agree field for field on real corpora, the four kb-media containers write identical envelope bytes and read identical receipts, the kba container (raw and adpcm tiers) and the kbb bank document match byte for byte on the real SoundFont, the kbi instrument converts both preset shapes byte-exact, and the mixer renders stems bit-identical through the same loop order and f32 widening. Round-trip and one-ulp contracts where the format or the platform does not allow byte equality, stated in the judges themselves: the kba lossless tier (stored-block zlib, not a zlib library's matching strategy), the ztdw config float tie, and the pan coefficients' one-ulp libm difference. The remaining half of the migration is the tool surface, not the kernel: rust-toolface's exec dispatch.

goals.title: The Rust tool surface: a registry that routes every op to the rust core or back to JS, and an exec dispatch
goals.notes: The registry lists the engine's 16 tools with the ops the Rust core has absorbed; selfcheck asserts the tool set against the TOOLS array in lib/core.mjs (16 against 16). The exec dispatch - turning an op id into a rust call or a js fallback - is the next half of this surface, and is what lets the thin shell route.

goals.title: The DSH plugin thin shell: spawn the Rust binary and forward the JSON tool surface
goals.notes: The borrowing direction flips: where KID once borrowed ffmpeg and opna, DSH will borrow KID's Rust binary. The plugin face stops importing core.mjs directly and becomes a process bridge with JSON forwarding. The judge for this surface will be a selfcheck section that drives an op through both routes and compares.

goals.title: The same-source WASM build for the browser and embedding surfaces
goals.notes: The Rust core compiles to WASM from the same source, so the browser face shares the decoder kernel rather than carrying a JS reimplementation. It follows the decoder kernel: once the family is ported, the WASM target reuses it.

goals.title: The Kohane Processing Bundle: stages 3-5 (composer with waterfall intake, mixing, volume window with asset conversion) are in
goals.notes: The sealed .kpb envelope is judged by the 8-20 percent content-volume window, the media self-proof replays a score through the synth, the mixer renders stems through a verified .kbm, and the asset conversion (sf2 to kbb, presets to kbi, ztdw probes) rides the same container family. The kb-media containers this goal produced are now ported to Rust under rust-core.

goals.title: The material side of the bundle: wavetable-versus-recording classification, art and doc disposition, the full SD-90 conversion volume, aupreset conversion
goals.notes: The remaining items are corpus-level: classify the Xfer wavetable set against recordings, decide where the art and manual corpus lands, measure the whole SD-90 conversion, and convert the .aupreset set. The ztdw container reader already probes the Heavier7Strings corpus and is the tool this goal leans on.

goals.title: An 8-16 bit music piece embeddable in an exe, on the SD-90 plus synths, fusing Hirasawa and ZUN styles
goals.notes: The piece is composed in KID itself, written through the composer and the .kbs/.kbw containers, rendered by the synth into a small embeddable stream (adpcm or raw tier), with SD-90 as the base instrumentation plus additional synth voices. The two FLP studies (Alice and Yu) feed the arrangement; Hirasawa's layering and ZUN's pentatonic turnarounds are the reference blend.

goals.title: LM4 Mark II integration: the 64-bit bridge is built, the drumkit indexing is in, the host-side test and the KID side remain
goals.notes: The kit parser reads the plain-text pad rows with the GM MIDI map and is ported to Rust against the real Wizoo kit. The 64-bit jBridge proxy pair (LM4-MarkII.64.dll as a Proxy64 copy next to the original 32-bit dll) is built and waits on the host-side GUI test in FL; the KID side then indexes the full content tree.
